problem.title_as_question: How can an adult player optimize elastic loading and timing on the forehand and serve?
problem.definition: Adult players often fail to produce effortless power because they grip too tightly and consciously steer the backswing, killing the elastic momentum and stretch needed on forehands and serves.

symptoms.description: The racket tip lacks inward momentum and fails to spring load in the back of the swing.
Swing timing feels rushed and awkward because the elastic spring has to be created in the tiny space right before contact.
The serve motion jackknifes downward with the player snapping over the top straight down into the net.

causes.statement: The racket tip does not have enough inward momentum during preparation to spring-load the wrist apparatus naturally.
The hitting hand and wrist are held too tight, actively pressing the racket and killing its elastic momentum.
The player attempts to consciously control and steer the back of the swing rather than trusting passive elasticity.
The racket fails to load into-out on the serve because there is insufficient stretch in the back of the drop.

angles.summary: Using inward racket tip momentum combined with pulling the handle forward creates an elastic spring load that increases ball speed without extra effort.
Side-by-side footage compares a serve that jackknifes straight down into the net against a serve that effortlessly slaps through with forearm stretch.
Directly cueing hip rotation often fails because players force hip movement without transferring the stored energy into the hitting apparatus.
Coaching the distal end allows players to directly feel the power apparatus and energy of the forearm whacking the ball.

solutions.summary: Push the hands away from the body outward in preparation to set up inward racket tip momentum.
solutions.external_goal: Push the hands away from the body out here in preparation.

solutions.summary: Keep the hand and wrist loose and relaxed in the back of the swing while pulling the handle forward.
Use the non-dominant left hand to drag the hitting hand onto the ball, especially on approach shots.
solutions.external_goal: Use that left hand to drag the hitting hand onto the ball.

solutions.summary: Focus on feeling the early stretch load the power in the back of the serve so that contact happens automatically.
Cue the swing by feeling the distal forearm loading rather than consciously forcing hip rotation.
